1) macrophages inhibit the growth of BFUs-E in vitro, and 2) this inhibition is mediated by TNF and GM-CSF.
macrophages suppress erythroid colony formation by releasing TNF alpha which acts in synergy with GM-CSF to suppress erythroid progenitor growth.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of hematopoietic progenitor cell growth in vitro.
the regulation of hematopoiesis by macrophages.
the effects of macrophages and macrophage-derived factors on the growth of hematopoietic progenitor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-1 alpha, TNF alpha, and GM-CSF act synergistically in vitro to regulate erythropoiesis.
macrophages suppress the growth of BFUs-E by the release of GM-CSF, which in turn stimulates macrophage release of TNF-alpha, which suppresses BFU-E growth in the presence of GM-CSF.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of TNF alpha to murine bone marrow in the presence of GM-CSF or IL-1 alpha results in the suppression of erythroid progenitors and stimulation of granulocytic and macrophage progenitors.
IL-1 alpha, TNF-alpha and GM-CSF can all suppress the growth of erythroid progenitor cells.

IL-1 alpha and TNF alpha are involved in the negative regulation of BFU-E growth in vitro.
